body_text: View All News Covista Earns Five National Honors Recognizing its Workplace Culture, Career Growth Opportunities and Commitment to Responsible Business July 20, 2026 Download (opens in new window) Awards highlight the company's investment in colleagues, students and the communities it serves CHICAGO--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Covista (formerly Adtalem Global Education), America's largest healthcare educator, today announced it has been recognized with five prestigious national awards honoring the company's workplace culture, employee experience and commitment to corporate responsibility. The recognitions confirm Covista as one of the best healthcare education companies to work for in the country, with honors from some of the most respected names in business media, including TIME, Forbes, Newsweek and U.S. News & World Report. The awards represent feedback from thousands of employees, job seekers and members of the public, and underscore Covista's ongoing investment in building a workplace where employees can grow, thrive and do meaningful work, while building a career. Covista offers faculty, staff and colleagues the opportunity to shape the future of healthcare through education, training the next generation of healthcare professionals across five accredited institutions. The company's 10,000 faculty and colleagues come from a range of backgrounds—business, academia, healthcare, government, nonprofits—all united in the company's vision to be the destination where healthcare ambitions are made possible. Honors Include: TIME World's Best Companies 2025 Covista was named to the inaugural TIME World's Best Companies 2025 list , which highlights leading global organizations that exemplify excellence in today’s corporate landscape. Companies were evaluated using three primary data sources: Employee Satisfaction, Revenue Growth and Sustainability Transparency. Out of hundreds of thousands of data points assessed, the top 1,000 companies were recognized for outstanding performance across these key areas. Forbes America's Dream Employers 2026 Covista was named one of America's Dream Employers 2026 by Forbes , based on an independent survey of college students and employees at companies with at least 1,000 U.S. workers over the past three years. More than 266,000 data points were gathered to determine how frequently Covista was named a “dream employer” and how likely employees are to recommend the company as a place to work. Newsweek's America's Most Responsible Companies 2026 Covista was included on Newsweek's list of America's Most Responsible Companies 2026 , which focuses on a holistic view of corporate responsibility that considers all three pillars of ESG: Environment, Social and Corporate Governance. The analysis is based on the quantitative data from more than 30 KPI across the three areas of ESG, and CSR reputation, derived from an extensive survey conducted among U.S. residents, assessing the public’s perception of each company's social responsibility efforts. Forbes America's Best Employers for New Grads 2026 Covista earned a place on the Forbes list of America's Best Employers for New Grads 2026 , recognizing companies where early-career professionals can build meaningful careers. The list was compiled from an independent survey of over 100,000 young professionals working for companies and institutions employing at least 1,000 employees in the U.S. from all industry sectors. U.S. News & World Report Best Company to Work For – Midwest Covista was named a 2026-2027 Best Company to Work For – Midwest by U.S. News & World Report . The rating evaluated nearly 3,900 public and private companies across factors including pay and benefits, work-life balance, job stability, workplace comfort and career development opportunities. "Being recognized across so many respected national rankings is a powerful validation of the culture we’ve worked hard to build inside and out," said Sara Hill, Chief Human Resources Officer, Covista. "These honors belong to our colleagues. Their trust, feedback and everyday commitment to one another and to our students is what earned Covista this recognition, and we’re proud to keep investing in the kind of workplace where people can do their best work and build highly impactful careers." The recognition also reflects Covista’s approach to creating a workplace where doing exceptional work and making a meaningful impact go together. A key part of this is Covista Open Doors , the company's multi-year impact commitment to build and sustain the healthcare workforce. Through complementary investments by Covista and the Covista Foundation , an independent 501(c)(3) public charity, the organizations have committed $10 million and 50,000 volunteer hours over the next five years. The investments advance a structured, three-part strategy focused on inspiring the next generation of healthcare professionals through career exploration programs and community partnerships; removing barriers for students through scholarships and emergency grants; and supporting the mental health and wellbeing of healthcare workers through evidence-based programs that address burnout and promote career longevity. "When our colleagues have the support they need to do their best work, that strength ripples into the classroom and out into the communities we serve," said Megan Noel, Chief Corporate Affairs Officer, Covista. "By investing in our people and our communities, we are building a more responsible business and a lasting contributor to education, healthcare and broader society." More information about Covista’s colleague experience and impact commitments can be found here . About Covista Covista (NYSE: CVSA) is America's largest healthcare educator, serving more than 100,000 students and supported by a community of 400,000 alumni across five accredited institutions. Through personalized, tech-enabled education powered by 10,000 faculty and colleagues, Covista expands access to healthcare careers and addresses the U.S. healthcare workforce shortage at scale. Covista is the parent company of American University of the Caribbean School of Medicine, Chamberlain University, Ross University School of Medicine, Ross University School of Veterinary Medicine and Walden University. For more information, visit covista.com and follow us on LinkedIn , Instagram and YouTube . Media Contact Nick Lucido nick.lucido@covista.com Source: Covista Inc. View All News

title: KNOX LANE COMPLETES ACQUISITION OF CROSS COUNTRY HEALTHCARE
summary: Knox Lane, a growth-oriented investment firm, today announced the completion of its acquisition of Cross Country Healthcare, Inc.
body_text: Appoints Joel Tremblay as Chief Executive Officer SAN FRANCISCO and BOCA RATON, Fla. — July 21, 2026 — Knox Lane, a growth-oriented investment firm, today announced the completion of its acquisition of Cross Country Healthcare, Inc. ("Cross Country Healthcare" or the "Company"), a leading technology-enabled healthcare workforce solutions company. In conjunction with the closing of the transaction, Joel Tremblay has been appointed Chief Executive Officer of Cross Country Healthcare. Kevin C. Clark, Co-Founder, Chief Executive Officer, and Chairman of the Board, will retire from his leadership roles and will support the Company and Mr. Tremblay to ensure a seamless transition. Mr. Tremblay brings nearly two decades of leadership experience across the healthcare workforce solutions industry. Most recently, he served as President of Medical Solutions, where he played a key role in building and scaling one of the nation's largest clinical staffing organizations. "I am honored to lead Cross Country Healthcare as it returns to private ownership and enters its next phase of growth,” said Mr. Tremblay. “With its trusted brand, leading market presence, and differentiated platform, the Company is uniquely positioned to help clients navigate workforce challenges and ensure access to quality patient care. As a private company, we will have an enhanced ability to invest in innovation, strengthen our capabilities, and deliver greater value to clients, healthcare professionals, and the communities we serve. I look forward to working alongside this talented team to build upon the Company's strong foundation and drive long-term growth." The completion of the transaction marks the beginning of a new era for Cross Country Healthcare as a privately held, standalone company focused on advancing workforce solutions through continued investment in technology, innovation, and operational excellence. As part of the transaction, Cross Country Healthcare's locums division has been acquired by All Star Healthcare Solutions, a portfolio company of Knox Lane. "Cross Country Healthcare occupies a distinctive position at the intersection of healthcare workforce solutions and technology,” said John Bailey, Managing Partner at Knox Lane and Shamik Patel, Partner at Knox Lane. “The Company has established a recognized market position, a trusted brand, and a differentiated platform designed to address critical workforce challenges across the healthcare ecosystem. We’re thrilled to work with Joel again and look forward to partnering with the entire Cross Country Healthcare team to accelerate innovation, expand capabilities, and create long-term value for clients, healthcare professionals, and stakeholders.” "I am incredibly proud of the Cross Country Healthcare team and everything that we have accomplished. For more than four decades, Cross Country has been committed to helping healthcare organizations address workforce challenges and ensure access to quality patient care,” said Mr. Clark. “This transaction marks an important next step for the Company's future, and I am confident Knox Lane’s strategic partnership and Joel’s proven leadership will support the Company’s growth and evolution. I look forward to seeing the organization build on its legacy of leadership while continuing to serve clients and healthcare professionals with excellence." Advisors BofA Securities, Inc. served as exclusive financial advisor to Cross Country Healthcare and delivered a fairness opinion to the Cross Country Healthcare Board of Directors. Davis Polk & Wardwell LLP served as legal counsel to Cross Country Healthcare. MTS Health Partners served as exclusive financial advisor to Knox Lane and Kirkland & Ellis LLP served as its legal counsel. About Cross Country Healthcare Cross Country Healthcare is a technology-driven healthcare workforce solutions company that helps healthcare organizations solve complex labor challenges. Through its staffing, advisory, and workforce technology capabilities, Cross Country supports health systems across nursing, allied health, and nonclinical service lines. Through Intellify, its workforce intelligence platform, Cross Country helps healthcare leaders gain greater visibility across workforce spend, supplier performance, labor demand, and operational execution, supporting faster decisions and stronger workforce outcomes. Learn more at www.CrossCountry.com and www.Intellify.com . About Knox Lane Knox Lane is a growth-oriented investment firm based in San Francisco, comprised of a team of accomplished investors and operators with a strong track record of partnering with leading companies to accelerate growth. Knox Lane employs an investor-operator mindset and provides support across human capital, brand management, AI and digital transformation, sourcing, supply chain and logistics, strategic acquisitions, and business development. For more information, visit www.knoxlane.com . title: Advance Bookings: How to Charge Card Details from Online Travel Agents
summary: Receive and charge customer or virtual cards from Booking.com or Expedia easily with Tab. Benefit from secure payments, reduced no-shows, and simple refunds. Learn more!
body_text: If you’ve received card details from Booking.com or Expedia, then we have a solution for you. Disclosure: OTA payment flows, virtual card rules, and fee references in this article are accurate as of May 18, 2026. Terms vary by OTA, country, and provider agreement. ‍ What types of cards might I receive? You can receive two types of cards from Booking.com or Expedia: You can receive the customer’s card details directly You can receive a Virtual Card (this is where Booking.com or Expedia have already charged the customer and is a way of them paying you) If you’re not sure, you can use the information here to work out which card you have. Some POS systems will allow you to charge cards remotely, but you should check how much they charge you for this. Virtual Cards in particular can be very expensive. ‍Sources: Booking.com partner documentation on virtual card flows, Expedia Group documentation on property-collect payments and card handling, PCI DSS guidance. Charging customer card details If you have a Tab account, you can charge secure customer card details provided by the OTA using our Advance Booking feature. You simply enter the customer details, including their card details, and click on ‘Take Payment’! Charging customer card details when you receive them has lots of advantages - it can reduce no shows and payment disputes, and helps you filter out booking fraudsters. We always recommend that you charge the card details when you receive the booking, securing the payment with your refund policy. For any unsuccessful payments, you can always send the guest a payment link. If they don’t pay, you know to cancel the booking and make the space available for legitimate guests. With Tab, you can easily manage refunds too (both in full and partial) - it’s easy, free, and we refund all fees. We charge 2.9% + 1 USD to process Advance Bookings. Like with our other payments, we charge a small customer fee because we convert the payment into a local payment for the customer, saving them expensive international fees from their bank. This means that Tab is usually cheaper for your customer too. Read more about why here . ‍ ‍ Charging virtual cards Charging Virtual Cards is even easier. Tab has a specific feature to charge Virtual Cards from a number of providers, not just Booking.com and Expedia. Simply enter the cards details and charge the card. This feature costs 7.9% + $1 USD per transaction (there is no customer fee) as Virtual Cards are more expensive to process, so we do recommend sticking to customer card details if you are given the option! ‍ Conclusion In summary, efficiently handling card payments from Booking.com or Expedia can streamline your operations and enhance your guest experience. By understanding the types of cards you receive and leveraging Tab's features, you can reduce no-shows, minimize payment disputes, and manage refunds effortlessly. Whether you're processing customer card details or Virtual Cards, Tab provides a secure and cost-effective solution tailored to your needs. title: Transocean Ltd. Announces $425 Million Additional Backlog for Ultra-Deepwater Drillship
body_text: Transocean Ltd. Announces $425 Million Additional Backlog for Ultra-Deepwater Drillship April 14, 2026 STEINHAUSEN, Switzerland, April 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Transocean Ltd. (NYSE: RIG) (“Transocean”) today announced that the Deepwater Corcovado was awarded a 1,156-day contract extension with Petrobras in direct continuation of its current activity. The extension is expected to contribute approximately $445 million in incremental backlog and commit the rig through November 2030. Prior to the extension period, from April 1, 2026, until the commencement of the new contract in September 2027 (approximately 525 days), the existing backlog will be reduced by approximately $20 million. About Transocean Transocean is a leading international provider of offshore contract drilling services for oil and gas wells. The company specializes in technically demanding sectors of the global offshore drilling business with a particular focus on ultra-deepwater and harsh environment drilling services and operates the highest specification floating offshore drilling fleet in the world. Transocean owns or has partial ownership interests in and operates a fleet of 27 mobile offshore drilling units, consisting of 20 ultra-deepwater floaters and seven harsh environment floaters. title: Reliability, Observability & Data Layer Improvements
body_text: We shipped bug fixes, better observability, and a refactored data layer for the Core Gateway. Fixes & observability Endpoints in Paused or Inactive state now activate correctly, and OSS default-user login no longer requires a license. We fixed filter evaluation for boolean values in arrays and a startup bug where the worker blocked the agent server. For Sentry, we've updated the configuration to use the default Environment field. Data layer improvements We refactored the data layer to use SQLC for type-safe SQL across API keys, configuration, delivery attempts, organisations, portal links, projects, sources, and filters. Behaviour is unchanged and no config or API changes are required on your side. Upgrade for the fixes and observability improvements.

title: Ravenna Review 2026: Honest Pros and Cons
summary: Read our honest Ravenna review for 2026, covering its pros, cons, features, pricing, ease of use, and top alternatives.
body_text: In April 2025, Ravenna announced a $15 million seed funding round led by Madrona Ventures and Khosla Ventures, positioning itself as a Slack-native internal help desk alternative to legacy systems like ServiceNow for mid-market companies. The platform aims to deliver faster deployment and modern user experiences compared to traditional enterprise ITSM platforms. For IT teams, HR departments, and operations leaders evaluating internal service management platforms, Ravenna represents an interesting option with genuine strengths in certain areas, particularly around identity and access management automation, but an honest review requires examining both what Ravenna does well and where meaningful gaps exist. This analysis draws on verified sources, competitive positioning data, and available customer feedback to help internal support teams make informed decisions about whether Ravenna's current capabilities align with their organizational requirements and risk tolerance. Key Takeaways Ravenna shows promise, but public review volume remains limited. With limited customer reviews publicly available, teams should avoid treating early feedback as mature market consensus for enterprise purchasing decisions. Pricing transparency may require additional review. Ravenna does not publish a full pricing page on its website, creating budget planning challenges and reducing comparison shopping leverage for IT and HR teams evaluating internal help desk solutions. Reliability should be reviewed carefully for mission-critical internal support. Teams evaluating Ravenna should ask for current uptime history, incident documentation, and Slack integration reliability details before committing. Identity and access workflow integrations are one area where Ravenna may fit teams focused on access request automation. Deep connections to Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, and Google Workspace make it appealing for teams prioritizing access request automation over broader internal service management. Organizations needing omnichannel intake, published compliance credentials, and proven customer validation may find better fit elsewhere. Alternatives like Unthread’s Slack-native ticketing may be a stronger fit for teams that need transparent pricing, multi-channel intake across Slack, Teams, email, and chat, and broader internal support automation across IT, HR, finance, procurement, legal, and workplace operations. What Ravenna Gets Right: Core Strengths Slack-Native Workflow Automation Ravenna's visual workflow builder allows IT and HR teams to create automations without code. The platform handles end-to-end orchestration across IAM, HRIS, MDM, and SaaS tools, with specialized agents that execute tasks across identity providers. For organizations where access requests dominate internal support volume, this focus creates clear value. The platform claims deployment in minutes rather than weeks, contrasting sharply with enterprise ITSM implementations that typically require months and consulting fees. For teams frustrated by portal friction and slow legacy systems, this speed-to-value proposition resonates. Identity Provider Integration Depth Ravenna's integration with Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, and Google Workspace goes beyond basic authentication. The platform automates employee lifecycle workflows including provisioning, access modifications, and offboarding across connected systems. MDM integrations with Jamf and Kandji extend this automation to device management. For IT teams where joiner-mover-leaver processes consume significant time, these vendor-maintained integrations reduce engineering burden. Ravenna handles API updates when providers change their interfaces, unlike approaches that generate code customers must maintain themselves. AI Resolution Tracking Ravenna's analytics explicitly track AI versus human resolution rates, showing which tickets the AI handled autonomously versus those requiring human intervention. This transparency helps IT and HR leaders understand their actual automation ROI rather than relying on vendor claims. The platform also offers dashboards for support volume, SLA breaches, and recurring issue patterns. For teams building business cases around AI investment, this visibility into deflection rates provides concrete metrics. Common Considerations for Ravenna Minimal Customer Validation The most significant concern for enterprise buyers is Ravenna's limited track record. The platform currently has minimal public customer validation, making early positive feedback statistically insufficient for serious enterprise evaluation. Compare this to established platforms with hundreds of reviews across multiple years. Available reviewer feedback explicitly notes the product feels "still early" and expresses hesitation about deploying for larger teams. Other comments mention waiting for automated workflows to fully launch. These candid assessments signal a platform still finding its footing rather than a battle-tested solution. For IT and HR teams supporting hundreds or thousands of employees, deploying a platform with limited customer validation introduces meaningful risk. Enterprise buyers in regulated industries need to validate provisioning automation and audit exports carefully. Pricing Transparency Gaps Ravenna does not publish a full pricing page on its website. While some third-party sources suggest approximate pricing in the $50 per agent monthly range for entry tiers, specific feature breakdowns by plan remain unclear without sales conversations. This can create additional evaluation steps for internal support teams: Budget planning may require sales conversations before finance review Comparison shopping requires multiple sales calls instead of straightforward evaluation Cost comparison may take longer without published pricing Additional costs may become clearer later in the evaluation process Organizations requiring procurement approval with defined budgets face additional friction. Teams that need to justify spend against alternatives may need additional details on pricing tiers and feature mappings. Reliability Considerations Teams evaluating Ravenna should ask for current uptime history, incident documentation, and Slack integration reliability details before committing. For a platform whose core value proposition is Slack-native AI automation, integration stability matters significantly. IT teams deploying internal help desks need confidence that employee requests will be handled reliably during critical periods. A single outage does not condemn a platform, but early-stage products typically experience more stability issues than mature alternatives. Slack-Focused Fit Ravenna primarily serves organizations deeply committed to Slack. Teams not using Slack extensively, or those with significant employee populations outside Slack, may not realize full value from the platform. This creates challenges for organizations with: Multi-channel intake requirements where employees submit requests via email, web portals, or Teams Hybrid environments where some departments use Slack while others do not External stakeholder interactions requiring unified service management across internal and external channels Future platform flexibility if communication tool preferences evolve ITIL Coverage Considerations Ravenna appears more focused on fast deployment and modern user experience than formal process governance. Organizations requiring full ITSM capabilities including CMDB, change management, problem management, and CAB approvals should verify whether the platform matches their governance requirements. The 2026 Enterprise Buyer's Guide notes that organizations in regulated environments should validate provisioning automation and audit exports carefully before committing. Ravenna's focus on speed may trade off governance features critical for compliance-driven IT operations. Knowledge Maintenance Questions Prospects evaluating Ravenna have cited concerns about knowledge base maintenance. Comments during evaluations reference documentation that "gets out of date really quickly" and challenges around maintaining accurate knowledge resources. While AI can help generate documentation, keeping it current requires systematic processes many early-stage platforms still develop. Comparing Ravenna to Established Alternatives How Established Alternatives Compare For organizations comparing Ravenna with more established internal help desk platforms, alternatives may address several evaluation areas: Transparent Pricing: Unthread publishes clear pricing at $50 per agent monthly for Basic and $75 for Pro plans, with explicit feature breakdowns. Teams can evaluate cost-per-agent against specific capabilities without sales conversations. Proven Customer Validation: Platforms with established review bases and multiple case studies across IT, HR, Legal, Procurement, and Finance teams provide confidence that comes from real-world deployment experience. Omnichannel Support: Unthread’s IT service desk handles requests across Slack, Microsoft Teams, email, web chat, and customer portals. Published Compliance: For regulated industries requiring HIPAA compliance or SOC 2 certification, platforms with published security credentials and available BAAs reduce vendor validation overhead. Broader Automation Coverage: While Ravenna emphasizes access request automation, some vendors support a broader range of internal support workflows across IT, HR, finance, procurement, legal, and workplace operations. Unthread's purpose-built AI agents span multiple Tier 1 internal support workflows, not just identity management. The Multi-Department Advantage Organizations using internal help desks across multiple departments benefit from platforms designed for broad internal service coverage. A single platform handling IT infrastructure requests, HR policy questions, legal review requests, procurement approvals, and facility management reduces tool sprawl and administrative overhead. Documented case studies show platforms achieving 40% automatic ticket resolution across IT, HR, Legal, Procurement, and Finance teams. This breadth differs from approaches optimizing primarily for access request deflection, which may show high automation rates on narrow use cases while leaving other departments underserved. Private Ticketing for Sensitive Requests HR teams often need to handle sensitive employee requests including payroll issues, parental leave, employee documents, benefits questions, and policy concerns. Platforms supporting private ticketing within Slack allow employees to submit confidential requests without leaving their communication environment. This capability matters for maintaining appropriate privacy around sensitive topics while preserving the convenience of Slack-based submission. Organizations should verify whether Ravenna's workflow automation extends to private HR use cases or focuses primarily on IT access management. Channel-Based Help Desk Configuration Effective Slack-native platforms can transform a specific channel like #it-help into a full internal help desk. This creates a single intake location for employee requests while allowing certain ticket types to remain in-channel and others to move to DMs or private flows. The ability to configure routing rules, escalation paths, and privacy settings without complex implementation distinguishes mature platforms from early-stage alternatives. Workflow automation that administrators can adjust easily as requirements change reduces ongoing maintenance burden. Who Should Consider Ravenna Ravenna may fit specific organizational profiles: Slack-Only Environments: Teams fully committed to Slack with no multi-channel requirements benefit most from Ravenna's Slack-native design. Access Request Focus: Organizations where identity management and access provisioning represent the majority of internal support volume may find Ravenna's integration depth compelling. Early Adopter Tolerance: Teams comfortable deploying emerging products and providing feedback that shapes platform development may accept maturity trade-offs in exchange for innovative features. ServiceNow Replacement: Mid-market companies frustrated by legacy ITSM complexity and seeking faster deployment may find Ravenna's modern approach appealing, though they should validate feature coverage carefully. Where Alternatives May Fit Better Several organizational profiles suggest alternatives would provide better fit: Multi-Channel Requirements: Teams needing unified service management across Slack, Teams, email, and web should evaluate omnichannel platforms. Regulated Industries: Organizations requiring published HIPAA compliance, SOC 2 certification, or detailed security documentation should verify credentials before committing. Budget Planning Needs: Finance teams requiring concrete pricing for procurement approval benefit from transparent published pricing. Risk-Averse Buyers: Organizations preferring proven platforms with established customer bases and extensive reviews reduce deployment risk by choosing validated alternatives. Full ITSM Coverage: IT teams needing CMDB, change management, problem management, and formal process governance should verify Ravenna's depth against requirements. The Verdict Ravenna represents an interesting entry in the AI-native internal service management market. Its Slack-native design, identity provider integrations, and visual workflow builder address real pain points for teams frustrated by legacy ITSM complexity. However, teams may still want to review Ravenna’s public customer validation, pricing details, reliability history, and Slack-focused approach before making an enterprise deployment decision. The "still early" characterization from existing reviewers aligns with typical patterns for recently funded platforms. For organizations requiring proven reliability, transparent pricing, omnichannel support, and established customer validation, alternatives like Unthread’s Slack-native ticketing may offer a more established path to AI-automated internal help desk capabilities. Unthread's self-learning knowledge base addresses documentation maintenance concerns, while AI analytics provide similar deflection tracking with deeper ITSM context. The decision ultimately depends on organizational risk tolerance, channel requirements, and whether identity management or broader internal support coverage drives primary value. Teams should request detailed demos, verify compliance credentials, and speak with existing customers before committing to any platform. Frequently Asked Questions How does Ravenna handle Microsoft Teams environments? While Ravenna mentions growing Teams support, its primary strength remains Slack-native functionality. Organizations with significant Teams populations should verify current Teams capabilities directly with Ravenna and compare against platforms offering native support across both environments. The platform's focus on Slack means Teams features may lag in development priority. What implementation support does Ravenna provide? Ravenna emphasizes rapid deployment taking minutes rather than weeks, but detailed implementation support structure remains unclear from public documentation. Enterprise buyers should clarify onboarding resources, dedicated support availability, and professional services options during evaluation. Compare this against alternatives offering documented implementation paths and dedicated solutions engineers. Can Ravenna integrate with existing ticketing systems? Ravenna's integration documentation focuses heavily on identity providers (Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace) and HRIS systems (BambooHR, HiBob, Rippling). Organizations requiring bidirectional sync with existing helpdesk platforms like Zendesk, Freshdesk, or Jira should verify specific integration capabilities. Some alternatives offer explicit bidirectional ticket synchronization for hybrid deployments. How does Ravenna handle SLA management and escalations? While Ravenna tracks SLA breaches in its analytics, detailed documentation on escalation configuration, notification workflows, and SLA customization requires sales conversation. Teams with complex SLA requirements across multiple service tiers should request specific demonstrations of these capabilities and compare against platforms with published SLA management features. What data residency and privacy controls does Ravenna offer? Enterprise buyers in regulated industries or specific geographic regions need clarity on data residency options, encryption standards, and privacy controls. Ravenna's public documentation does not detail these aspects as comprehensively as established platforms. Organizations should request security documentation, compliance certifications, and data processing agreements during evaluation.

title: Navigating a Defining Moment in Biotech to Advance Global Growth in 2026 and Beyond
summary: Acadia outlines its 2026 strategy to build a global neuroscience and rare disease biotech through precision medicine, data innovation, and patient-driven growth.
body_text: The biopharmaceutical industry is at a pivotal moment. Scientific advances are accelerating, but so are patient expectations and technological advancements, while access to treatment is increasingly being impacted by rapidly-shifting regulatory policies and priorities. These global realities are reshaping what it takes to advance a therapy from discovery to delivery. For Acadia, these factors serve to clarify our priorities for 2026 and beyond: build a global neuroscience and rare disease company designed for sustained growth, which turns scientific promise into meaningful innovation for underserved neurological and rare disease communities around the world. That focus means staying disciplined in where and how we invest. We are prioritizing neurological and rare diseases where unmet need remains high, advancing a pipeline built for long-term impact, and strengthening the capabilities required to operate at global scale. Equally important, we are grounding our decisions in scientific rigor, responsible use of data and technology, and close engagement with patients and caregivers, ensuring that innovation is shaped not only by what is possible, but by what truly matters to the communities we serve. Building Long-Term Growth in Neurological and Rare Diseases We are building sustainable growth across a focused portfolio in neurological and rare diseases. Our growth is built on the strong foundation of our core commercial franchise, made up of approved treatments for Parkinson’s disease-related hallucinations and delusions and for Rett syndrome. These therapies have established our credibility as a company willing to take on some of the most complex conditions. From that solid footing, we are advancing a robust late-stage pipeline that targets large, underserved populations. This includes programs in Alzheimer’s disease psychosis, Lewy body dementia (LBD) with psychosis, and major depressive disorder – conditions that collectively affect millions of people and remain inadequately treated. These programs represent significant opportunities to apply precision medicine innovation at scale in neurological disorders. For example, we are embedding exploratory biomarkers in both our Alzheimer’s disease psychosis and LBD trials to help understand whether certain patient subsets respond better to treatment. These biomarker results could help inform our trial design – and ensure that any product we launch can be as specific and targeted to the appropriate patient populations as possible. At the same time, we are investing in an innovative early-stage pipeline that positions us for long-term impact. Our disclosed programs span essential tremor, tardive dyskinesia, Rett syndrome and Fragile X, Huntington’s disease, and SYNGAP1-related disorders, alongside multiple undisclosed programs. Together, these reflect a deliberate balance between near-term opportunity and future innovation. Supporting this growth are four core drivers of transformation critical to our strategy: Precision Medicine, including an increasing focus on biomarkers from the earliest stages of development. Data Innovation, involving transforming how we discover and develop medicines through digital tools, artificial intelligence, and machine learning. Globalization, building targeted capabilities beyond the United States (including in markets across Europe, Japan, and Canada) to meet patient needs at global scale. Patient Empowerment, creating a connected ecosystem of patients, caregivers, and advocates to turn lived experience into actionable insight. How Are We Turning Transformation Drivers into Action? Biotech leadership is earned through decisive execution, not aspiration alone. We are converting ambition into real-world action and measurable impact. A clear example is our decision to develop a new powder-for-oral-solution formulation of our approved treatment for Rett syndrome, which will be available on a limited basis starting in the first quarter of 2026 with broader availability anticipated in the second quarter. This innovation, which provides caregivers with greater flexibility to modify the taste and volume of their loved one’s dose, was informed directly by feedback from patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers about what would make a meaningful difference in daily care. By responding to the community’s feedback, we aim to offer greater flexibility and choice while maintaining the therapeutic integrity patients rely on. We are also investing in strong data governance frameworks and fostering a culture of accountability, where every colleague understands their role in maintaining data integrity and quality. As we increasingly harness technology and data, this foundation is essential – not only to enable responsible, AI-driven innovation, but to preserve trust with patients, regulators, and partners. Meeting the Moment Through Science, Technology, and Transparency The external environment for the biopharmaceutical industry is changing rapidly, and Acadia is meeting this moment head-on. Pricing pressures continue to intensify, requiring discipline and focus. Patients and families are demanding greater transparency and treatments that reflect their lived experiences, not just clinical endpoints. Advances in genetics, biomarker science, and artificial intelligence are also transforming what is possible in understanding and addressing disease. These forces are not separate from our strategy. They are shaping it. We are building a pipeline and organization designed to thrive in this reality, integrating patient insight, precision science, and responsible innovation. Across our pipeline, momentum is building. We have eight disclosed programs and multiple undisclosed programs, with five additional Phase 2 or Phase 3 study initiations expected by the end of 2026, and four Phase 2 or Phase 3 study readouts anticipated by the end of 2027. Artificial intelligence is accelerating this progress. In commercial operations, AI-powered analytics help our teams better target engagement. In R&D, clinical command centers monitor trials in real time to identify and mitigate risk. In regulatory functions, AI-enabled medical writing expands internal capacity and accelerates document development. Across these applications, technology is supporting better decisions, faster learning, and greater impact. A Transformative Year Ahead Looking ahead, 2026 represents a transformative year for Acadia. We expect key regulatory opinions that will mark important steps in our global expansion efforts, including for our Rett syndrome treatment. We also anticipate continued progress across our late-stage neurological disease programs, including emerging therapies for Alzheimer’s disease psychosis. More broadly, this year will focus on deepening our mission: transforming scientific possibility into real-world impact. The road ahead will not be simple. The science is complex, the challenges are real, and the stakes are high. But that is exactly why we are here. By staying focused on patients, investing in our core capabilities, and executing with discipline and purpose, I believe Acadia is well positioned to become a biotech powerhouse – one defined not just by growth, but how we can truly be the difference in people’s lives.
